prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The SNP’s 2015 manifesto pledges to make Scotland stronger at Westminster with a louder, progressive voice that ends austerity, protects public services and delivers shared prosperity. A vote for the SNP is a vote to shake up an out‑of‑touch Westminster, lock the Tories out if there is an anti‑Tory majority, and press any Labour government to deliver real change—not a Tory copy. This election is not about independence; it is about rebalancing the UK’s priorities so Scotland and the whole UK benefit.

Economic and fiscal plan: replace deeper cuts with modest, responsible increases in public spending; invest in infrastructure, skills and innovation to create more, better‑paid jobs; and reduce debt as a share of income each year. Fund fairness by asking the wealthiest to contribute a little more—restore the 50p top rate; levy banks and bankers’ bonuses; introduce a mansion tax; end non‑dom status; and crack down on avoidance. Seed‑capitalise a Scottish Business Development Bank; back small firms with higher Employment Allowance and prompt‑payment protections; cut and devolve Air Passenger Duty to boost tourism; expand export finance; and invest in housing (100,000 affordable homes a year UK‑wide), high‑speed rail to and from Scotland, superfast broadband and 4G. Create a Sovereign Wealth Fund from natural resources.

Fair work and living standards: raise the UK minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020 (with better youth and apprentice rates), promote the Living Wage, and support collective bargaining and modernised trade union balloting. End exploitative zero‑hour contracts through consultation.

Public services and welfare: increase NHS funding (delivering an extra £2bn for Scotland by 2020‑21), protect the health service from privatisation, and integrate health and social care. Expand free childcare to 30 hours for all 3–4 year‑olds and eligible 2 year‑olds; keep university tuition free; grow Modern Apprenticeships to 30,000 a year; extend Educational Maintenance Allowance. Scrap the Bedroom Tax; halt and reform Universal Credit and PIP rollout; reverse DLA-to-PIP changes; raise the work allowance by 20%; overhaul sanctions and Work Capability Assessments; increase Carer’s Allowance to JSA level. Protect pensioners with the triple lock, a £160 single‑tier pension, Winter Fuel Allowance, and a review of raising state pension age beyond 66. Cut energy bills by reforming obligations and enforcing wholesale price pass‑through.

Security and foreign policy: oppose renewing Trident and redirect savings; strengthen conventional capabilities (including maritime patrol aircraft) and transparency in MoD spending; support veterans. Back 0.7% aid focused on poverty, create an LGBTI rights envoy, support a two‑state solution, and ensure military action meets UN Charter tests. Keep Scotland and the UK in the EU; require a “double majority” for any UK exit; protect public services in trade deals.

Environment and communities: match Scotland’s ambitious carbon targets; back offshore and onshore wind, hydro, CCS and community energy; maintain a fracking moratorium; enhance species protection. Devolve broadcasting; secure a fair BBC Scotland budget share; protect Royal Mail’s universal service; reform Westminster with STV, abolish the Lords, votes at 16 and real MP recall. Secure Home Rule by delivering Smith in full and going further—devolving employment, welfare, business taxes, NICs and equality—moving to full financial responsibility with Barnett in transition.

An SNP vote will make Scotland’s voice heard—loudly—and deliver fairer, more progressive politics across the UK.
